items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: Fred McClelland, my roommate, he’d say “I like this guy’s saxophone playing.”

ctx.x: What was it about jazz music at the time that became — that you were so enamored of?

I don’t know. Words probably, the words are pretty good and they had a message to them. And Fred McClelland, my roommate, he’d say “I like this guy’s saxophone playing.” He explained to me the difference in sound on a record between a trumpet and a clarinet and a sax. And there was one funny sound that we used to get at that time, and he said “I wonder if that’s a bassoon?” Neither one of us knew. But one time he said “I met (some uncle) up in Twill the other day and he had an old instrument in there and I blew…
